samples.summary: Live grow now repositions the editing container for text inside a transformed group, where the commit deliberately writes nothing — new drift + snap-back
samples.evidence: The new `if (isGrow)` left/top tracking fires whenever `isGrow` is true, and `isGrow` is driven only by `autofit`/`growMode` (text-box-editor.ts:325); editor.ts:4357 passes `growMode: 'auto'` for EVERY text element, including one nested in a rotated/scaled group. But the editor's grow gate is stricter: editor.ts:4304 sets `editingGrowApplicable = target.kind === 'text' && !ancestorHasTransform`, and the commit at editor.ts:4418 skips the frame write entirely when `ancestorHasTransform`. `frame` handed to the mount is `target.editFrame` (editor.ts:4337 → buildEditTarget at editor.ts:7558), which is the WORLD frame, so for a text box inside a rotated group its rotation is non-zero and `resizeFrameToSize` returns a shifted x/y. Consequence for that path: while typing, the editing container now translates across the slide, while (a) the canvas underlay does not move (maskEditingElement is passed `liveHeight = null` because `editingGrowApplicable` is false, editor.ts:1541) and (b) the committed frame never moves — so the surface drifts away from the box and snaps back on commit. Before this change the container only changed height. Fix belongs on the new code: gate the left/top tracking on the same ancestor-transform condition the commit uses (e.g. a new mount option mirroring `editingGrowApplicable`).

samples.summary: Table row/column insert & delete still patch frame.w/h alone on a possibly-rotated table, contradicting the new "all size writers must anchor" contract and the design doc's exhaustiveness claim
samples.evidence: `resize.ts` now documents "Callers that write `w`/`h` on a rotated frame must go through this (or `resizeFrameWorld`) rather than patching size alone", and docs/design/slides/slides-format-options-panel.md:246 claims the autofit-grow commit is "the one other such caller". It is not: MemSlidesStore mutates size with x/y pinned at memory.ts:1381 (`e.frame = { ...e.frame, h: e.frame.h + height }`, insertTableRow), memory.ts:1407 (insertTableColumn), memory.ts:1487 (deleteTableColumn), and the Yorkie mirror repeats it at packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:2320 and :2344. On a rotated table these produce exactly the #1039 jump. Pre-existing behaviour, but it leaves the newly stated invariant and the design-doc note inaccurate.

samples.summary: `anchoredFramePatch` silently overwrites caller-supplied x/y in any patch that also touches w/h, while `onCommitFrame`'s type still advertises a free `Partial<Frame>`
samples.evidence: `return { ...patch, x: next.x, y: next.y }` puts the computed x/y LAST, so a patch such as `{ x, y, w, h }` loses its explicit position. Today the only producers are size-position-section.tsx:102 (`{ w: px }`), :118 (`{ h: px }`) and :169 (`{ rotation }`), so nothing is broken now, but the prop contract at size-position-section.tsx:36 (`onCommitFrame: (ids, patch: Partial<Frame>) => void`) permits combined patches and the next caller that sends one will be silently ignored. Spreading the anchor first (or only filling x/y when absent) would keep the advertised contract.

verdict.reason: All claimed code exists and the path is reachable. text-box-editor.ts:495-506 repositions container left/top on every live grow, gated only on `isGrow` (text-box-editor.ts:325), which editor.ts:4357 sets for EVERY text element via growMode 'auto'. The mounted `frame` is the world frame (editor.ts:4337 → buildEditTarget editor.ts:7548-7559 with insetFrame preserving rotation at 7544; world composition in model/group.ts:403-428), so rotation is non-zero for text inside a rotated group and resizeFrameToSize (resize.ts:118-131) returns shifted x/y. Meanwhile the editor's stricter gate (editor.ts:4295-4304) makes editingGrowApplicable false for transformed ancestors, so the underlay gets a null live height (editor.ts:1541) and the commit skips the frame write entirely (editor.ts:4418) — live container drift with no underlay movement and a snap-back on commit. Reachable: dblclick drills into groups (editor.ts:4124-4148) and enterEditMode resolves group-nested text with no rotated-ancestor bail-out (editor.ts:4219-4247), unlike the table branch at 4167-4169. This is an invariant/contract mismatch with a module outside the diff, i.e. in-lane, and the visible drift/snap-back is major.

finding.summary: Live autofit-grow underlay still grows h with x/y held fixed, so it no longer matches the committed anchored frame on a rotated text box
finding.evidence: `maskEditingElement` renders the in-edit text box's decoration with `{ ...el.frame, h: Math.max(MIN_TEXT_BOX_H, liveHeight) }` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:7436), driven every keystroke from `render()` at :1541. That is exactly the size-only growth the delta removed from the commit path: it grows about the unrotated top-left in local terms, i.e. it moves the painted centre of a rotated box. Since the commit now anchors the unrotated top-left instead (`:4431`), the live preview and the committed render for a rotated text box differ by the compensation vector, so the box fill/border visibly jumps at commit — the same #1039 symptom, just moved to the preview→commit transition. Fix belongs on the preview: build the live frame with `resizeFrameToSize(el.frame, el.frame.w, liveHeight)`.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `maskEditingElement` builds the live underlay frame as a size-only spread (`{ ...el.frame, h: Math.max(MIN_TEXT_BOX_H, liveHeight) }`). That code does not exist in the repository. At packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:7440-7447 the live clone is built as `liveHeight !== null ? resizeFrameToSize(el.frame, el.frame.w, Math.max(MIN_TEXT_BOX_H, liveHeight)) : el.frame` — i.e. exactly the anchored construction the finding proposes as the fix, sharing the same `resizeFrameToSize` helper used by the commit path at editor.ts:4431. The surrounding comment (editor.ts:7432-7439) explicitly documents that a size-only clone would drift from the committed frame and jump at commit (#1039), and that this was avoided. The render driver at editor.ts:1537-1542 passes `lastEditingContentHeight` into that same anchored path, so there is no other construction site. A grep for size-only frame spreads across packages/slides/src turned up only unrelated x/y translation sites (drag.ts:170,175; editor.ts:5699; slide-size.ts:39), none touching the in-edit underlay. A test also pins the claimed-broken behaviour: packages/slides/test/view/editor/rotated-autofit-commit.test.ts:139-158 asserts the masked live frame keeps the unrotated NW corner fixed in world space (`live.x` is NOT 400) and equals the committed frame. The premise of the finding is therefore factually not present.

finding.summary: Panel rotate-90 still reads frame.rotation unguarded, so the legacy missing-rotation case this delta hardens against persists NaN rotation from the same panel
finding.evidence: The delta's premise (resize.ts:87-100, frame-patch.ts doc block, docs/design/slides/slides-format-options-panel.md:256) is that a legacy/imported frame can lack `rotation` and that persisting a NaN geometry field makes the element vanish. `rotate90` in the same format panel computes `((el.frame.rotation + delta) % (Math.PI * 2) + Math.PI * 2) % (Math.PI * 2)` and writes it straight through `store.updateElementFrame(..., { rotation: next })` (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/format-panel/index.tsx:162-165). With `rotation` absent this stores `rotation: NaN` — a strictly worse outcome than the x/y NaN the new `Number.isFinite` guard in `frame-patch.ts` was added to prevent, reached from the neighbouring control in the same panel. Note packages/frontend has no tsc lane, so nothing else flags this.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `rotate90` in packages/frontend/src/app/slides/format-panel/index.tsx computes `((el.frame.rotation + delta) % (Math.PI * 2) + Math.PI * 2) % (Math.PI * 2)` and writes it through unguarded, persisting NaN for legacy frames lacking `rotation`. That code is not present. The actual implementation (index.tsx:168-172) derives `const base = Number.isFinite(el.frame.rotation) ? el.frame.rotation : 0;` and uses `base` in the modulo expression, with an in-place comment (index.tsx:162-167) explicitly naming the legacy/imported missing-rotation hazard and the `anchoredFramePatch` parallel. A missing or non-finite rotation therefore yields a finite result (0 + delta normalized), never NaN, so `store.updateElementFrame(..., { rotation: next })` at index.tsx:173 cannot persist NaN. A Grep for `rotation` across the entire format-panel directory shows the guarded form is the only read of `el.frame.rotation` on this path; the only other rotation write, size-position-section.tsx:169, passes the rotation control's own committed radian value rather than deriving from `el.frame.rotation`, so it is not the described site either. The premise files exist as described (frame-patch.ts:19-25 doc block, frame-patch.ts:33 finite check), but the alleged bypassing site is already guarded in the same lines the finding cites as unguarded.
